key_insight: A de-biased VLM judge can be used not just to rank single-image-to-3D results, but to probe where lightweight adaptation of a strong public generator actually changes geometry versus merely improving appearance.
engineering_relevance: For practical 3D pipelines, the paper shows that cheap PEFT on public data may preserve parity with the base model, so meaningful gains likely require stronger supervision or targeted conditioning fixes rather than generic fine-tuning.
method: Use separate training and evaluation judges to avoid circularity.
Apply position-bias correction and harden the judge against image overload, geometry-hiding renders, and reference-free scoring.
Test multiple adaptation methods, input regimes, and degradation severities on TRELLIS furniture generation.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports strong calibration for the judge (clear-gap win-rate 0.83–1.0, base-vs-base about 0.5) and evaluates methods with directional win-rates on n=8 objects, finding no method reaches the 65% target.
watch_item: Results are limited to small directional comparisons on furniture and public-data, lightweight PEFT, so stronger or broader improvement may not generalize without more data or model capacity.
paper_title: Judging to Improve: A De-biased VLM-as-3D-Judge Protocol for Single-Image 3D Generation
